steps.title: Prepare all required solutions
steps.instruction: Prepare the following buffers and reagents exactly as described:

substeps.instruction: 50 mM alk‑16: dissolve 14.0 mg alk‑16 in 1 mL DMSO.
PBS (1 L): dissolve 8 g NaCl (137 mM), 0.2 g KCl (2.7 mM), 1.44 g Na₂HPO₄ (10 mM), 0.24 g KH₂PO₄ (1.8 mM) in ultrapure water, adjust pH to 7.3 with HCl, bring to 1 L.
RIPA buffer (1 L): mix 10 mL Triton X‑100 (1 % v/v), 10 g sodium deoxycholate (1 % w/v), 1 g SDS (0.1 % w/v), 8.78 g NaCl (150 mM), 50 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 7.4 (50 mM), add water to 1 L.
1 % SDS lysis buffer (1 L): mix 10 g SDS (1 % w/v), 8.78 g NaCl (150 mM), 50 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.4 (50 mM), add water to 1 L.
4 % SDS buffer (1 L): mix 40 g SDS (4 % w/v), 8.78 g NaCl (150 mM), 50 mL 1 M TEA pH 7.4 (50 mM), add water to 1 L.
HEPES buffer (1 L): mix 8.78 g NaCl (150 mM), 50 mL 1 M HEPES pH 7.4 (50 mM), add water to 1 L.
2 M NH₂OH solution (10 mL): dissolve 1.39 g NH₂OH·HCl in 8 mL ultrapure water, adjust pH to 7.4 with NaOH, bring to 10 mL.
5 mM azido‑rhodamine stock: dissolve 34.3 mg azido‑rhodamine in 10 mL DMSO.
50 mM TCEP solution: dissolve 14.3 mg TCEP in 1 mL ultrapure water.
2 mM TBTA stock: dissolve 10.6 mg TBTA in 10 mL 1:4 (v/v) DMSO:t‑BuOH.
50 mM CuSO₄·5H₂O solution: dissolve 12.5 mg CuSO₄·5H₂O in 1 mL ultrapure water.
4× SDS‑PAGE loading buffer (100 mL): mix 8 g SDS (8 % w/v), 20 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl pH 6.8 (200 mM), 40 mL glycerol (40 % v/v), 0.4 g bromophenol blue (0.4 % w/v), add water to 100 mL.
Destaining buffer (1 L): mix 500 mL methanol (50 % v/v), 100 mL acetic acid (10 % v/v), 400 mL ultrapure water (40 % v/v), mix thoroughly.

steps.title: Seed cells for labeling
steps.instruction: Plate adherent cells in 12‑well plates (or 60 mm dishes) in normal growth medium (e.g., DMEM + 10 % FBS) and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to reach 70‑80 % confluency.

steps.title: Optional transfection (12‑well)
steps.instruction: In a microcentrifuge tube, dilute 1 µg plasmid DNA in 100 µL Opti‑MEM, add 2.5 µL ViaFect, mix gently, incubate 15 min at room temperature, then add dropwise to the well. Incubate 6 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Metabolic labeling with alk‑16
steps.instruction: Replace the culture medium with fresh DMEM containing 2 % charcoal/dextran‑treated FBS and 50 µM alk‑16 (or an equal volume of DMSO for control). Add media gently, then incubate 16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Harvest and wash cells
steps.instruction: Discard medium, add 1 mL ice‑cold PBS, pipette up/down to resuspend, centrifuge 4,000 × g for 2 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant. Repeat PBS wash once more. Collect cell pellet and either proceed immediately or freeze in liquid N₂ and store at –80 °C.

steps.title: Lyse cells for proteome analysis
steps.instruction: Add 50 µL 1 % SDS lysis buffer to each pellet, supplement with EDTA‑free protease inhibitor cocktail and 0.2 µL benzonase (50 U). Vortex vigorously, then centrifuge 12,000 × g for 20 min at room temperature. Transfer supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Quantify and aliquot protein
steps.instruction: Determine protein concentration by BCA assay. Aliquot equal amounts (e.g., 100 µg) into 1.5 mL tubes and adjust volume to 50 µL with 1 % SDS lysis buffer. Add 39 µL HEPES buffer to bring total volume to 89 µL.

steps.title: Prepare click reaction cocktail
steps.instruction: In an Eppendorf tube combine sequentially: 10 µL 5 mM azido‑rhodamine (in DMSO), 25 µL 2 mM TBTA (in DMSO/t‑BuOH), 10 µL 50 mM TCEP (in H₂O), 10 µL 50 mM CuSO₄·5H₂O (in H₂O). Vortex thoroughly. Keep solutions fresh and protect azido‑rhodamine from light.

steps.title: Perform click reaction on lysates
steps.instruction: Add 11 µL of the click cocktail to each 89 µL lysate sample, vortex, and incubate in the dark at room temperature for 2 h (duration may be shortened to 1 h if desired).

steps.title: Precipitate proteins with methanol
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL ice‑cold methanol to each reaction, mix, and store at –20 °C overnight.

steps.title: Centrifuge and wash protein pellets
steps.instruction: Centrifuge 20,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant, then wash the pellet twice with 1 mL ice‑cold methanol (invert gently, centrifuge 20,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C each wash).

steps.title: Air‑dry protein pellets
steps.instruction: Leave the tubes open on the bench for 60 min at room temperature until pellets are completely dry.

steps.title: Resuspend pellets and optional NH₂OH treatment
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 57.5 µL 4 % SDS buffer, shake 15 min at 1,500 rpm (use a bath sonicator if needed). Add 12.5 µL 2 M NH₂OH (optional; if not required, add 70 µL 4 % SDS buffer instead).

steps.title: Add loading buffer and reduce disulfides
steps.instruction: Add 25 µL 4× SDS‑PAGE loading buffer and 5 µL bond‑breaker TCEP solution, heat at 95 °C for 5 min, vortex briefly, then centrifuge 1 min at 10,000 × g at room temperature.

steps.title: Run SDS‑PAGE and visualize fluorescence
steps.instruction: Load 20 µg protein per lane onto a 4‑20 % Bis‑Tris gel, run 1 h at 140 V. Destain gel by rocking 1 h in destaining buffer at room temperature. Scan gel on a ChemiDoc MP imager using “rhodamine” mode. Afterwards, stain the same gel with Coomassie Brilliant Blue to confirm equal loading.

steps.title: Seed cells for POI labeling
steps.instruction: Plate cells in 60 mm dishes with normal growth medium as in the first seeding step and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Transfect POI plasmid (60 mm)
steps.instruction: In a microcentrifuge tube, dilute 4 µg plasmid DNA in 400 µL Opti‑MEM, add 10 µL ViaFect, mix gently, incubate 15 min at room temperature, then add dropwise to the dish. Incubate 6 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.

steps.title: Metabolic labeling for POI
steps.instruction: Perform the same labeling step as described in “Metabolic labeling with alk‑16” (replace medium with DMEM + 2 % charcoal/dextran‑treated FBS containing 50 µM alk‑16, incubate 16 h at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂).

steps.title: Harvest and wash POI cells
steps.instruction: Harvest cells as described in “Harvest and wash cells” (two PBS washes, centrifugation, pellet collection).

steps.title: Lyse cells for POI analysis
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL RIPA buffer to each pellet, supplement with EDTA‑free protease inhibitor cocktail and 0.4 µL benzonase (100 U). Vortex, rotate 30 min at 4 °C, then centrifuge 12,000 × g for 20 min at 4 °C. Transfer supernatant.

steps.title: Quantify protein and adjust concentration
steps.instruction: Measure protein concentration by BCA assay. Aliquot 600 µg of protein into 2.0 mL dolphin tubes and bring volume to achieve 1.5 mg/mL with RIPA buffer.

steps.title: Immunoprecipitate tagged POI
steps.instruction: Wash anti‑HA/GFP/FLAG agarose beads with PBS, then add 20 µL bead slurry per 600 µg lysate. Rotate 2 h at 4 °C. Centrifuge 8,000 × g for 1 min at 4 °C, discard supernatant. Wash beads three times with 1 mL chilled RIPA (rotate 5 min at 4 °C each, centrifuge 8,000 × g 1 min 4 °C). Then wash three times with 1 mL chilled PBS (same conditions). Resuspend beads in 44.5 µL PBS.

steps.title: Click reaction on immunoprecipitated beads
steps.instruction: Add 5.5 µL freshly prepared click cocktail (same composition as before) to the bead suspension, incubate in the dark for 2 h at room temperature. Afterwards, wash beads three times with 1 mL RIPA buffer (rotate 5 min at 4 °C, centrifuge 8,000 × g 1 min 4 °C).

steps.title: Prepare bead samples for SDS‑PAGE
steps.instruction: Resuspend washed beads in 17.25 µL ultrapure water, 7.5 µL 4× SDS‑PAGE loading buffer, and 1.5 µL bond‑breaker TCEP solution. Add 3.75 µL 2 M NH₂OH (optional; if not required, add 21 µL ultrapure water instead). Heat 95 °C for 5 min, vortex, then centrifuge 1 min at 8,000 × g at room temperature to pellet beads. Collect supernatant.

steps.title: SDS‑PAGE fluorescence gel for POI
steps.instruction: Load 20 µL of the supernatant onto a 4‑20 % Bis‑Tris gel, run 1 h at 140 V. Destain gel 1 h in destaining buffer, then scan on ChemiDoc MP (rhodamine mode).

steps.title: Prepare second gel for western blot
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL 1× SDS‑PAGE loading buffer to the remaining bead sample, vortex, centrifuge 1 min at 8,000 × g at room temperature. Load 20 µL onto a second 4‑20 % Bis‑Tris gel, run 1 h at 140 V. After electrophoresis, transfer proteins to a nitrocellulose membrane and detect the POI by standard western blotting (e.g., anti‑HA).

description: Validation of protocol This protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research article: Xu et al. [7]. Chemical Proteomics Reveals N ε -Fatty-Acylation of Septins by Rho Inactivation Domain (RID) of the Vibrio MARTX Toxin to Alter Septin Localization and Organization. Mol Cell Proteomics. Rho inactivation domain (RID) from Vibrio cholerae and Vibrio vulnificus efficiently catalyzes the covalent attachment of long-chain fatty acyl groups (e.g., palmitoyl, stearyl) to the ε-amino group of lysine residues on substrate proteins in host cells [7, 10] ( Figure 3A ). To globally profile RID-mediated N ε -fatty acylation, HeLa cells were transfected with either wild-type RID (RID-WT) or the inactive mutant RID-C2835A (RID-CA), incubated with alk-16 overnight, and then lysed. Proteins in the lysates were subjected to click chemistry with azido-rhodamine for in-gel fluorescence analysis, as described in parts I and II ( Figure 3B ). To reduce interference from S -palmitoylated proteins, lysates were treated with NH 2 OH to selectively cleave thioester bonds. The in-gel fluorescence revealed specific alk-16 labeling of many proteins in RID-WT lysates, but not in RID-CA lysates ( Figure 3C ), indicating that RID mediates N ε -fatty-acylation of these host proteins in living cells. To further validate that RID mediates the N ε -fatty-acylation of Ras-related protein Rac1 (RAC1), an in-gel fluorescence assay was performed. Specifically, HEK293T cells were co-transfected to express RID and HA-tagged RAC1, followed by labeling with alk-16. Cell lysates were subjected to immunoprecipitation, click-reacted with azido-rhodamine, and analyzed by in-gel fluorescence after NH 2 OH treatment, as described in parts III and IV ( Figure 4A ). The results showed that RAC1 was labeled by Alk-16 only in the presence of RID-WT, but not upon expression of RID-CA ( Figure 4B ), confirming that RID catalyzes the N ε -fatty acylation of RAC1.
